not_gradable.why: creates the order row and then calls Stripe. WireCall is on the SECOND live Stripe secret key on this machine, the one OutRip and MatchLine also carry. It runs here with a placeholder so its own unconfigured path runs; what that path leaves behind is in the defects instead.

the first leg of the double opt in. The house sender renders the body through a production edge function BEFORE it looks for a Resend key, and then needs a live key to send. Nothing here may send real mail, so the outbound firewall refuses it and the route answers its own 500. The SECOND leg, /api/subscribe/confirm, is a graded task.

a read. Every reward reads database rows, so a route that writes none has nothing to grade. It is exercised on every /history page load and its pass gate is checked from the row side by grant-the-wire-pass.

the handshake, not an act a person performs. Its only writes are the player row it mints when a key is missing and a last_seen_at stamp, and both happen on every page load. It is driven by the browser rollout and its minting behaviour is what the-named-device guards against.

not_gradable.what: buildSlate, the other half of scripts/tick.mjs
not_gradable.why: it reads whatever FrontWire and Popwire hold at that instant and writes a new slate from them. Both tables belong to other products and frontwire-desk truncates one of them on this stack, so the rows it would produce are not this environment's to pin. The fixture already holds today's slate, so the tick's build half reports the product's own idempotence and does nothing.

the schema has it, the board prints it in preference to the generated tag, and the Wire Pass is sold on a named leaderboard entry. Nothing in the product writes it, so setting a name is not a task. It is a defect, below.

defects.summary: The Wire Pass webhook takes the player from the event metadata and never checks it against wc_orders.player_id, so an order can be marked paid while the pass lands on a device that did not buy it. Measured against the running copy: a signed checkout.session.completed naming order ...f5601 (owned by player ...f5003) with metadata player_id ...f5004 answered 200, marked ...f5601 paid, and granted season_pass plus the payer's address to ...f5004. The payer, whose order is now paid, holds no pass, and nothing anywhere reconciles the two rows.
defects.where: src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:41-51. Fixed in wirecall 2026-09-19: the webhook reads the order's own player_id and refuses a mismatch.

defects.summary: wc_players.display_name has no writer anywhere in the product, and the Wire Pass is sold on "a named spot on the leaderboard". It appears in a SELECT in src/lib/device.ts, in the /api/device response and in the board view, and in no INSERT or UPDATE in any of the seven routes, three library writers or the cron. Measured on production: 0 of 650 player rows carry one. The only name a player can have is the generated caller_tag, the first four hex characters of their uuid, and production already has 3 tags shared by more than one player at 650 rows, so two paying players can render as the same board entry.

POST /api/device inserts a wc_players row on every anonymous call with no rate limit, and the crawl guard cannot see it: src/middleware.ts excludes api/ from its matcher. That guard exists because other products on this estate took 149,991 and 719,915 crawler hits in a day, and this is the one route that WRITES on an unauthenticated call. Measured against the running copy: 25 POSTs with an empty body took wc_players from 6 rows to 31. Production holds 650 player rows, 1 of which has ever scored.

A failed checkout leaves a permanent pending wc_orders row carrying the buyer's email address. The route inserts the order before it calls Stripe and the catch block returns 500 without touching it; there is no failed status, no expiry and no cleanup path. Measured against the running copy with Stripe unreachable: 3 POSTs to /api/checkout answered 500 three times, wc_orders went from 3 rows to 6 and wc_players from 6 to 9, and all three new orders read pending with a null stripe_session_id and the address stored.
defects.where: src/app/api/checkout/route.ts:65-103. Fixed in wirecall 2026-09-19: the catch deletes the pending row it created.

defects.summary: The wc_players_leaderboard_read policy is unreachable and is one grant away from exposing every scoring player's email address. It is a row level policy for anon and authenticated using (points > 0 or streak_best > 0) on a table that holds email, and anon holds no grant at all, so the read is refused. The refusal PostgREST returns is the hint "Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT SELECT ON public.wc_players TO anon;", which is exactly the change that would turn the dead policy into a public read of ?select=email. The board does not need it: wc_leaderboard already answers 200 and selects six columns, none of them the address.
defects.where: pg_policies wc_players_leaderboard_read on public.wc_players. Fixed 2026-09-19: dropped in the shared project by migration wc_players_drop_dead_leaderboard_policy, and the environment's 03-rls.sql follows it.
